drivingQuestion: Why may a Jew bless a flame he lit from a gentile's, while a gentile lighting from a gentile may not be blessed?
outcomeNote: The Gemara concedes that the flame is essentially renewed and that the ban on a gentile lighting from a gentile is a rabbinic decree.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גּוֹי שֶׁהִדְלִיק מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִדְלִיק מִגּוֹי מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו. גּוֹי מִגּוֹי — אֵין מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו.
segments.en: «The Sages taught» in a baraita: «A gentile who lit» a candle «from» a candle that was in the possession of «a Jew or if a Jew lit» a candle «from a gentile, one may recite a blessing over it» at the conclusion of Shabbat. However, «if a gentile» lit a candle «from a gentile, one may not recite a blessing over it.»

segments.he: מַאי שְׁנָא גּוֹי מִגּוֹי דְּלָא — מִשּׁוּם דְּלֹא שָׁבַת? אִי הָכִי, יִשְׂרָאֵל מִגּוֹי נָמֵי הָא לֹא שָׁבַת!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What is different» about a candle that «a gentile» lit «from a gentile, that» one may «not» recite a blessing over it? «Because» the light «did not rest» on Shabbat. «If so,» the light of «a Jew» who lit a candle «from a gentile also did not rest» on Shabbat.

segments.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא הַךְ אִיסּוּרָא אֲזַל לֵיהּ, וְהָא אַחֲרִינָא הוּא, וּבִידָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל קָא מִתְיַלְדָא — אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא: הַמּוֹצִיא שַׁלְהֶבֶת לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים — חַיָּיב. אַמַּאי חַיָּיב? מַה שֶּׁעָקַר לֹא הִנִּיחַ, וּמַה שֶּׁהִנִּיחַ לֹא עָקַר!
segments.en: «And if you say» that «this prohibited» flame «has gone and this» flame «is a» new and «different» one which «came into being in the possession of a Jew,» as a flame is not a concrete, static object, but rather it constantly recreates itself; «however, this» halakha «that was taught» in a Tosefta in tractate Shabbat states: «One who carries out a flame» from the private «to the public domain» on Shabbat «is liable» for carrying out from one domain to another. If the flame is constantly recreating itself, «why is he liable? That» flame «which he lifted» from the private domain «he did not place» in the public domain «and that which he placed he did not lift.» One is only liable for carrying out on Shabbat if he lifted an object from one domain and placed that same object in another domain. Since one who carries out a flame on Shabbat is considered liable, evidently, despite any change that it may undergo, the flame is essentially considered a single entity.

segments.he: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם דְּאִיסּוּרָא נָמֵי אִיתֵיהּ, וְכִי קָא מְבָרֵךְ — אַתּוֹסֶפְתָּא דְּהֶתֵּירָא קָא מְבָרֵךְ, אִי הָכִי, גּוֹי מִגּוֹי נָמֵי!
segments.en: «Rather, actually that prohibited» flame «is also extant, and when one recites the blessing, he recites the blessing over the permitted addition» to that flame. The Gemara asks: «If so,» even if «a gentile» lit a candle «from a gentile as well,» the flame should be considered essentially new; one should be able to recite a blessing over the addition.

segments.he: אֵין הָכִי נָמֵי, גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם גּוֹי רִאשׁוֹן וְעַמּוּד רִאשׁוֹן.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Yes, it is indeed so.» Fundamentally, there is no reason to prohibit doing so. However, the Sages issued «a decree because of the first gentile,» who did not light the flame from another gentile, «and the first pillar» of flame that was kindled on Shabbat. Consequently, they prohibited all somewhat similar cases, including when a gentile lights a flame from another gentile.

moves.summary: a baraita on blessing a flame lit across the Jew–gentile line
moves.about: a baraita on which transfers of flame between a Jew and a gentile may be blessed at the close of Shabbat

moves.summary: if the reason is that the flame did not rest, a Jew lighting from a gentile should be barred too
moves.about: if the disqualification is that the flame did not rest, a Jew who lit from a gentile should be disqualified equally

moves.cueHe: וכי תימא הך איסורא אזל ליה
moves.summary: floats: the forbidden flame is gone and a new one is born in the Jew's hand
moves.about: a Tosefta making one liable for carrying a flame from the private to the public domain on Shabbat

moves.cueHe: אלא הא דתניא: המוציא שלהבת לרשות הרבים
moves.summary: one is liable for carrying out a flame, so a flame is one continuous entity
moves.about: rejecting the floated defence that the forbidden flame has gone and a new one is born in the Jew's hand, since one is liable for carrying out a flame

moves.summary: the forbidden flame persists; the blessing is over the permitted increment
moves.about: the prohibited flame does persist, and the blessing is recited over the permitted increment added to it

moves.summary: then a gentile lighting from a gentile should be permitted too
moves.about: if the blessing is over the permitted increment, a gentile lighting from a gentile should be permitted too

moves.cueHe: אין הכי נמי, גזירה משום גוי ראשון ועמוד ראשון
moves.summary: granted in principle; the ban stands only as a decree because of the first gentile and the first pillar of flame
moves.about: conceding the point in principle: the ban is only a rabbinic decree because of the first gentile and the first pillar of flame
